packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-03 — unverified image reading

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading. This is a blind reading. I have not tried to identify work or author.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

Observations
- Three overviews (image-001, -004, -007) plus one of a fourth face (image-010): four faces of what looks like a small paper bifolium or folded sheet, about 22 cm wide by 16.5 cm tall as photographed (ruler in frame), with a vertical central fold, many small holes (worm/insect damage and larger losses on the face in image-007/010), and adhesive/repair strips along the fold and along one outer edge.
- Text is upright in all overviews. Each written face carries a single text block that begins well to the right of the left edge (roughly at 1/3 of the sheet width) and runs across the central fold to the right edge; i.e. the lines are written straight across the fold, so the fold is later than the writing or the sheet was written flat. Wide blank margin at left and blank space below the text.
- Face A (image-001/002/003): a first block of 10 lines, a blank interval, then a second block of 7 lines, two of which (its lines 3-4) are indented. Paragraph signs of a looped "C"/"q" shape open both lines 1 and 5 of the second block.
- Face B (image-004/005/006): one continuous block of about 20 lines, the top line trimmed (only descenders remain).
- Face C (image-007/008/009): one block of about 16 lines, top-left torn away, ink much paler, many holes.
- Face D (image-010/011/012): no writing of its own that I can see; only faint show-through of face C. Sewing thread and a guard strip at the right edge.
- At the far left edge of faces A and C a narrow strip carries line-ends of another text column or leaf (a stub), cut vertically: single letters/syllables only.
- Script: a very rapid, highly abbreviated cursive in grey-brown ink, single hand as far as I can tell. No rubrics, no running titles, no enlarged or coloured initials, no underlining, no interlinear glosses seen. Frequent oblique strokes "/" used as punctuation after citations.
- The sign "ff" recurs many times, as does "l." and "C." followed by short abbreviated tags.

Tentative interpretation (not observation)
- The "ff … / l. … / C. de …" strings look like legal allegations (citations by title and opening word), so this is probably juristic prose: notes, a repetitio/lectura-type passage or collected notabilia. Face B reads like a list of parallel cases linked by "sic et …" (so also …). I do not infer author, work, date or provenance.
- Order of the faces is not established by the images; I label them A-D only by image sequence.

2. SPANS SELECTED / UNREAD
Selected: all of face A upper block (10 lines) and lower block (7 lines); all of face B (20 lines; my most secure reading); face C lines where ink survives (partial). Unread: the cut stub letters at the left edge of faces A and C (fragments only, listed at the end); face D (show-through only, nothing legible).
The hand is extremely abbreviated. Where I give a word in full it is usually an expansion; I mark expansions in ( ) and doubt with ?. Words I could not resolve are [illegible], and these are far more numerous on face A and C than on face B. A raking-light or higher-contrast image of face C, and a wider view of the left stub, would help.

3. TRANSCRIPTION

FACE A, upper block — image-002 (lines counted from the top of image-002; image-001 is the overview of the same face)

image-002 L1:  ff de lega(tis) p(rim)o [hole] [illegible] maior(is)? ro(n)is? i(n) ul(timis) volu(n)tat(ibus) q(uam) i(n)
image-002 L2:  (con)tractu(s)? et l(eg)e? [illegible, over the repair strip] de ul(timis)? volu(n)t(atibus)? / ad (con)tractu(s) et a(r)g(uitu)r? [raised letters at line end, "m"/"in"?]
image-002 L3:  de (con)tractu ad ul(timas) volu(n)tates l. si? / C. de lega(tis)? / dicit(ur)? i(n) co(ntrariu)m?
image-002 L4:  ro(n)e? (con)tractu(s)? et l(eg)e? [illegible] [hole] de (con)tractu ad ul(timas) volu(n)tat(es)? et a(r)g(uitu)r? [raised letters]
image-002 L5:  de ul(timis) volu(ntatibus)? [two holes] ad (con)tractu(s) l. pactu(m)? ff de pact(is) / si? i(n) dubio? [hole]
image-002 L6:  aut(em)? sp(eci)e? i(n)? l. maior(is)? intell(ec)t(us)? i(n)sp(icitur)? ul(time) volu(n)t(ates)? favora(bili)or(es)? l.
image-002 L7:  i(n) testa(men)to ff de reg(ulis) iur(is) / que(m)admod(um) alia multa su(n)t
image-002 L8:  sp(eci)alia i(n) quib(us) (con)tract(us)? (dif)fer(un)t? [illegible] i(n) ul(timis) volu(ntatibus)? / sive? tradit(i)o?
image-002 L9:  l. [illegible] ff de [illegible] / q(uo)d? l. [illegible, hole] i(n) (con)tractib(us) (et) q(ui)d(em)? [illegible] l.? C. de
image-002 L10: pact(is) / sic(ut)? [illegible] [hole] [illegible] su(n)t vel alia su(n)t? /

Note: L2 and L4 seem to repeat the same phrase pattern ("de ultimis voluntatibus ad contractus" / "de contractu ad ultimas voluntates"); the word(s) I render "et arguitur?" could equally be "et e(con)tra" or similar. I cannot settle it from the image.

FACE A, lower block — image-003 (lines counted from the top of image-003; its first two lines are also the cropped last two lines of image-002 = overlap, not additional text)

image-003 L1:  [paragraph sign] Co(n)tra(riu)m? o(ste)n(ditu)r? [illegible] p(rim)o? [illegible] / [illegible] [illegible] d(e)finit? de [illegible]

image-003 L7:  [illegible] ult(im)o? dedit p(ro)t(es)tat(em)? al(i)e(nandi)? s(ed)? [illegible] [illegible] no(n) sol(um)?

The lower block of face A I could read only in fragments; the letter-forms are clear in the image but the abbreviations are too compressed for me to expand responsibly. L5 has a visible ink blot or smeared deletion over one word in mid-line.

FACE B — image-005 (upper tile) and image-006 (lower tile); image-004 is the overview. Lines counted from the top of each tile. image-005 L13-L16 = image-006 L1-L4 (overlap).

image-005 L1:  [top line trimmed; only descenders visible]
image-005 L2:  q(uod) licet [illegible] / [illegible] / dicat q(uod) id q(uo)d [hole] s(er)v(u)s? (con)suev(i)t acquirer(e)? acquir(i)t?

statut(is)? [see next line]
image-005 L7:  statut(is)? licit(is)? et honest(is)? dic(itu)r? hodie? i(n) ro(…)? (con)s(…)? [illegible]
image-005 L8:  [illegible] / l. [illegible] / si? q(uis)? sup(er)? v(er)bo? (con)sue(tudine)? i(n) si(…) suo [illegible]

image-005 L15: corrig(er)e filios l. p(rim)a? C. de eme(n)d(atione) p(ro)pi(n)q(uorum) ubi? [illegible] q(uo)d p(ate)r
image-005 L16: [cropped at tile edge; = image-006 L4]

image-006 L1:  [= image-005 L13, top cropped]

image-006 L5:  licitu(m) e(st)? corrig(er)e uxore(m) ex ca(usa) legittima ymo flagellis et
image-006 L6:  fustib(us) p(otes)t [hole] [illegible] [hole] v(er)berar(e)? aut(entica)? s(ed) novo iur(e)

image-006 L8:  corrig(er)e mo(n)achu(m)? [illegible] et? [two holes] [illegible] et ibi no(tatu)r? q(uod) sic
image-006 L9:  d(omi)n(u)s domus p(otes)t corrig(er)e familia(m) sua(m) ut possit i(n)carc(er)ar(e)? [a small "re"/"tur"? written below the line end]

Gist of face B as I read it (tentative, from the legible words only): a chain of parallel statements about who may correct/chastise whom — master and slaves, husband and wife, teacher and pupils ("scolares"), father and sons, [abbot?] and monk, head of household and "familia" — each followed by a legal allegation, preceded by a passage on what a slave or son "is accustomed to acquire" for master or father. I supply nothing beyond the visible words.

FACE C — image-008 (upper tile) and image-009 (lower tile); image-007 is the overview. Ink very pale, top-left torn off, holes throughout. image-008 L11-L14 = image-009 L1-L4 (overlap).

Face C is given as isolated words only; I could not obtain connected sense, and the fault lies partly in the pale ink and losses and partly in my inability to resolve this hand's abbreviations at this contrast. The tokens "potuit deberi", "valet non", "generi", "mariti in testa(mento)" are the firmest.

FACE D — image-010, -011, -012: no text of its own seen. Faint reversed show-through of face C in the area right of the fold; not legible.

LEFT-EDGE STUB (faces A and C; image-002, -003, -008, -009): cut line-ends of a different block, one to four letters each (e.g. image-002 "…ud", "…r", "…so", "…ib(us)", "…lib(us)?"; image-008/009 "…q(ue)", "…ib(us)", "…f", single "o"/"e" forms). Not enough to read.

4. LIMITATIONS
- Top line of face B is trimmed; face C has lost its upper-left corner and has many holes; holes also interrupt most lines of faces A and B near the fold.
- The hand is an extreme legal cursive. Many of my expansions (especially on face A and all of face C) are guesses at abbreviation, flagged with "?". Readings in the face B list (image-005 L9 to image-006 L9) are the most reliable.
- Order of faces and whether the text is continuous from one face to the next are not established.
- A wider view of the left stub and an enhanced image of face C would be worth requesting.
- This is an unverified image reading.
